summary: Adding parameters to __init__ lets you give an object its starting values in the same line that creates it. Default values let you still create an object with no arguments.
notes: name="" is a default value. It is used only when you leave that argument out.
Student("Maya", 10, 3.8) matches the arguments to the parameters in order.
Student("Leo", 9) leaves out gpa, so it uses the default 0.0.
pitfall: Writing a second def __init__ replaces the first one. Then Student() causes TypeError: Student.__init__() missing 3 required positional arguments.
